_comment: Quality eval expectations for the threat-composer-app-browser-extension fixture.
Kept as data rather than code so that retuning a band is a reviewable one line
change instead of a patch to Python.
Reference runs, all on strands-agents 1.53.0 and
global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5. Runs 1 and 2 used the fixture before the Vite
migration was squash merged; run 3 used the fixture at the pinned commit below:
threats  mitigations  assumptions  total tokens  wall clock
Bands are wide on purpose, and those two runs are why. Same input, same model,
same code: mitigations moved by 19% and token spend by 34%. Pinning anywhere
near run 1's figures would have failed run 2 for no reason at all. A band's job
is to catch collapse or runaway, not to pin a figure, so each is set roughly
_fixture: The eval's input, held still so that the agent is the only thing that moves.
Without this the eval cannot do its job: if the fixture drifts, a score change
means either the agent regressed or the input changed, and the result cannot
tell you which.
Two mechanisms, because they do different jobs and neither substitutes for the
other.
commit    supplies the source. The workflow checks this commit out and
analyses that, so the eval keeps producing comparable numbers no
matter what later happens to the fixture on main. Without it, the
first person to edit the browser extension would stop the eval
running at all, which is close to the opposite of what it is for.
tree_sha256  verifies the source. Cheap defence against getting the wrong
tree anyway, whether through a checkout misconfiguration, a local
edit, or a pin left stale. Checked before the CLI runs, so a
mismatch costs nothing rather than a full inference run.
The hash covers relative paths and file bytes for 41 files: everything git
tracks apart from .wxt/, plus nothing untracked. tests/eval/test_fixture.py
asserts the hashed set matches what git tracks minus that documented exception,
so the exclusions cannot silently diverge from the repository.
.wxt/ is committed but excluded. The package
declares postinstall: wxt prepare and clean: rm -rf .output .wxt, so pnpm install
rewrites it. Hashing it made the pin depend on whether an install had run: a fresh
checkout gave 49 files and CI, after installing, gave 50. The agent does read
those files, so the pin is not a complete description of the input, but their
content derives from configuration that is hashed, and once commit is set the eval
reads committed content without installing.
commit is the squash merge of the Vite migration (#346) on main. The fixture
there differs from the pre-merge branch the bands were first measured on, so
run 3 re-measured it; its figures fall inside the existing bands, which were
left unchanged.
To reproduce the pinned fixture locally:
git worktree add /tmp/fixture <commit>
python -m threat_composer_ai.eval.quality --target /tmp/fixture/<path> ...
Changing the fixture is allowed, but deliberate. Re-run, sanity check the new
figures, then update commit, tree_sha256 and the bands together in one
reviewable change.
_default_settings: Settings that must come from the CLI's own defaults for a run to count as
measuring default behaviour. Asserted against the provenance the CLI records in
run-metadata.json, so this is a direct check rather than an inference.
This exists because the most likely cause of a quality change is a change to a
default: a new default model, a retuned timeout, an edited prompt. Pinning the
model in the eval would make it blind to exactly that. The eval follows the
default so that when the default moves, the effect on output is measured.
aws_region is deliberately not listed. It is deployment configuration rather
than behaviour, and in CI it necessarily comes from the environment because
credentials and model access are region scoped.
_allow_incomplete_threats: Number of threats permitted to leave grammar fields empty. Zero to begin with,
on the basis that the schema models the grammar and the agent should fill it.
Raise it if the reference run shows this is unrealistically strict rather than
_max_total_tokens: Cost regression guard, at roughly double the reference run. Nothing in the
artifacts notices a prompt change that doubles spend, and at roughly a million
tokens a run that is worth catching.
_telemetry: require_spans asserts telemetry actually produced spans. Without it, every
tool assertion below passes vacuously the moment telemetry breaks, which is
worse than not having them. expected_tools are the tools the workflow cannot
_concept_groups: Ideas any competent threat model of this extension ought to raise. Each group
holds alternative phrasings and matches if ANY one appears, case-insensitively.
That is deliberate: a model says 'background service worker' one run and
'background script' the next, so exact strings would fail for reasons that have
These groups were chosen over weaker signals such as CSP or DOMPurify, which
appeared once each in the first reference run and would make the check brittle.
min_concept_groups is 6 of 8, leaving room for phrasing to drift while still
failing if the output collapses into text that would fit any codebase.
